adjudicated.jp: 世界は美しい。
adjudicated.en: The world is beautiful.
comments: Much of this opening monologue is dripping with sarcasm. Taichi's just gotten off a really harsh time, and that's why he's diving into reminiscence. This part may just be a less hysterical version of the events of Another Story. For this sentence here in particular, it has to be reminded that what Taichi likes are unmoving and unchanging things to admire from a distance... despite how he's attracted to things that move. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The short declarative judgment and its positive evaluation are preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: ここから街を眺め渡すたび、なにをとち狂ったかそう思う。
adjudicated.en: Every time I pass my gaze over the town from up here, something that must be very wrong inside makes me think so.
comments: Yet, that "very wrong thing" is not necessarily his ultramarine; that he finds the world beautiful despite everything is something he can hang on to. More curious that "every time". How many times has he been here now? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rendering preserves the recurring act of surveying the town and reaching the preceding judgment, but converts the narrator's self-mocking 'what possessed me' phrasing into a diagnosis that something inside is wrong. The basic event remains recoverable while the voice is overexplained.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the self-directed incredulity without positing an internal defect.

adjudicated.jp: でも美しいものはしょうがない。
adjudicated.en: But when something is beautiful there are no ways to deny it.
comments: Shoganai will be consistently rendered as "no ways to", see CCX0001 for reason. The Shoganais are rare compared to the Shikatanais, possibly intentionally to remind of the ending. Well, both are rare, maybe they're just too bland for the author. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: しょうがない presents beauty as something that cannot be helped. 'No ways to deny it' shifts that resigned idiom into a claim about denial, though the concession remains broadly recognizable.
adjudicated.remedy: Retain the sense that its beauty simply cannot be helped.

adjudicated.jp: 青々とした夏の大気。
adjudicated.en: It's the lush atmosphere of Summer,
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the lush summer atmosphere. Capitalizing the season is mechanical rather than semantic.

adjudicated.jp: 一言で形容してしまうのが惜しいほど優美で。
adjudicated.en: so gracefully elegant that to describe it in a few words is to disappoint it.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the sight is so elegant that reducing it to a single description would feel regrettable or wasteful. The English instead says that description disappoints the object, adding an unsupported interpersonal relation and weakening 一言's compression to 'a few words.'
adjudicated.remedy: Describe an elegance too rich to reduce to a single phrase.

adjudicated.jp: 峠からの眺望は、いつもそんな所感を抱かせる。
adjudicated.en: Those are the feelings that the view from this ridge always arouses in me.
adjudicated.assessment: The view from the pass and the feelings it invariably prompts are preserved. 'Ridge' is contextually plausible, if less exact than 'pass.'

adjudicated.jp: ひそやかに息づく木々の合間からは、山々によって外界から隔絶された白い建物群が見えた。
adjudicated.en: From the break between the quietly breathing trees one could see a flock of white buildings, isolated from the outside world by mountains.
comments: flock=gun, same 'gun' as in 'gunjou', see also CCC3025 for more. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The visible white group of buildings, the trees, and the mountains' isolating function are all present. 'A flock of white buildings' is a conspicuously strained image for 建物群, so the result is source-complete but stylistically unstable.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an ordinary collective noun for the buildings while retaining the surrounding image.

adjudicated.jp: 街だ。
adjudicated.en: It's a town.
adjudicated.assessment: The identifying fragment is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 真新しく清潔、かつ閑静な地方都市……のはずれ。
adjudicated.en:
A brand new, pure, immaculate, and quiet suburban
city... 's rear end.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese describes the outskirts of a brand-new, clean, quiet regional city. The English turns 地方都市 into 'suburban city,' renders はずれ as the anatomically comic and grammatically detached 'rear end,' and redundantly splits 清潔 into 'pure, immaculate.'
adjudicated.remedy: Identify the location as the outskirts of a new, clean, quiet regional city.

highlights.text:
A brand new, pure, immaculate, and quiet suburban
city... 's rear end.

adjudicated.jp: つまりはしっこだ。
adjudicated.en: In short, this is just the appendix.
comments: see what I did there -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: はしっこ means an edge, end, or fringe. 'Appendix' names an attached supplement or organ and is not an English equivalent in this locative context.
adjudicated.remedy: Call it the edge or outskirts.

adjudicated.jp: 市の本体はというと、激険しい山を挟んで向こう側にある。
adjudicated.en: If one is looking for the main body of this city, it lies on the opposite side of these incredibly steep mountains.
adjudicated.assessment: The city's main body, its position on the far side, and the intervening steep mountains are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ちなみに向こう側にはデパートもあり、時間さえかければ都心にも出られる路線がそのつま先を置き、レンタルショップはおろかゲーセン・本屋・飲み屋・出張（ヘルス）まである。
adjudicated.en: Speaking of this other side, there's department stores, and if one takes the time, the routes that lead to the city center will lay at one's feet rental shops of course, and game centers, and book stores, and even "health services" shops.
comments: They're "massage parlors". Those are not scare quotes; they are an actual part of the name. And they will play a part, however weird, in the VN. Most famous ones are PeachLand and MateBook. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source lists amenities on the far side and says a rail line reaches toward the city center if one is willing to spend the time. The English attaches the rental shop to what the route 'will lay at one's feet,' omits the drinking establishment, pluralizes and redistributes items, and converts an outcall adult service into ordinary 'health services' shops. The resulting syntax also obscures the list's structure.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the rail-line clause separate and reproduce the full amenity list, including the drinking establishment and outcall adult service.

highlights.text: Speaking of this other side, there's department stores, and if one takes the time, the routes that lead to the city center will lay at one's feet rental shops of course, and game centers, and book stores, and even "health services" shops.

adjudicated.jp: 飽食の極みを迎えた文明の、爛熟した果実がここにある。
adjudicated.en: There it lies, the over-ripened fruit of a civilization that welcomes the heights of appetite.
comments: Appetite, see CCA0021 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 飽食 is satiation or overabundant consumption, not appetite. The source characterizes a civilization that has reached the extreme of surfeit; the English reverses this into welcoming appetite.
adjudicated.remedy: Refer to a civilization at the height of overconsumption or surfeit.

adjudicated.jp: 通称『都会』。
adjudicated.en: Alias a City.
comments: Capitalized, will be referred to this later. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rendering gestures toward an alias but is defective English and loses 通称's ordinary 'commonly known as' relation. The quoted label is also weakened by the indefinite article.
adjudicated.remedy: State that it is commonly known as 'the City.'

adjudicated.jp: さて、こっち側。
adjudicated.en: So then, about this side.
adjudicated.assessment: The discourse turn back to this side is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 民家が山のようにある。
adjudicated.en: There's residences, and mountains of them.
adjudicated.assessment: The large number of private homes and the mountain comparison are preserved. The number agreement is defective but does not change the content.

adjudicated.jp: 山も山のようにある。
adjudicated.en: Also mountains, and mountains of them.
comments: badum-tish. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The wordplay about having mountains in mountain-like quantities is recognizably preserved.

adjudicated.jp: あと学校がある。これは一つしかない。
adjudicated.en: And there's also a school. Just one, and no more.
comments: Important, since all other students must necessarily go to the school on the other side of the mountains (by train), ergo Nanaka can't go to another school on this side. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Both the presence of a school and the fact that there is only one are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 他に目立ったものといえば、大自然ぐらいのものか。
adjudicated.en: As for other things that jump to the eye, there are only the things of nature perhaps.
adjudicated.assessment: The tentative observation that little else stands out besides abundant nature is preserved, albeit in awkward English.

adjudicated.jp: 都会に傅き、そのおこぼれで日々を営み、馬車馬のように働く人民を迎え、送り出し、時には生みだし（大人のジョーク①）、夜は優しくも高らかに眠らせあげるのである。
adjudicated.en: Those people who work like horses, carrying on their days with the leftovers of the city they manserve, are here welcomed, sent off, occasionally brought into the world (adult joke #1), and put to very sound sleep at night.
comments: Curiously a hospital is never ever mentioned. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The city-dependent workers, their horse-like labor, the welcoming and sending off, the birth joke, and nightly sleep are all represented. However, 'the city they manserve' is malformed, the town's sustained agency becomes unstable, and 優しくも高らかに is compressed into the different idiom 'sound sleep.'
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the town as the clear agent throughout and preserve both the gentle and resounding qualities of the final joke.

adjudicated.jp: 要するにベッドタウンだ。
adjudicated.en: In other words, it's more of a dormitory than a proper town,
comments: I'll try to only tweak terms if they don't google to something relevant. This is particularly interesting for one reason: somehow Mutsumi lives in a dormitory, leaving Taichi unattended for days at an end... but the town itself is all but a dormitory. Very odd. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ベッドタウン is the established Japanese borrowing for a bedroom community or commuter town. The English instead calls the place a dormitory and adds the contrast 'than a proper town,' which the source does not state.
adjudicated.remedy: Identify it as a bedroom community or commuter town.

highlights.text: In other words, it's more of a dormitory than a proper town,

adjudicated.jp: 同じ市なのに。
adjudicated.en: despite being the same township.
adjudicated.assessment: The paradox that both sides belong to the same municipality is retained. 'Township' is a marked and jurisdictionally inexact choice for 市 in this context.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'city' or 'municipality' consistently with the surrounding passage.

adjudicated.jp: 深い政治的事情がありそうだ。
adjudicated.en: Seems there are some deep political circumstances.
adjudicated.assessment: The speculative suggestion of deep political circumstances is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: なお地図上では、二つの地を分断するこの雄峰、『丘』ということにされている。
adjudicated.en: According to the map, the majestic mountain ridges that cleave this territory in two are labeled hills.
comments: The mountains are religion, specifically Christianity, and the politicians (AKA those Of The World) call religion a small trifling little thing; a hill. And then Christianity is curry and therefore the message of Cross Channel is that politicians think mountains are curry. That doesn't seem too unlikely, by the way. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source points to this singular majestic peak, which separates two places and is designated a 'hill' on the map. The English pluralizes the peak into ridges, changes two places into one territory split in two, and pluralizes the map label.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the singular peak, the two separated places, and the singular cartographic label.

highlights.text: According to the map, the majestic mountain ridges that cleave this territory in two are labeled hills.

adjudicated.jp: どう見てもそんな可愛らしい代物ではない。
adjudicated.en: However you look at it, that is no sweet little affair.
adjudicated.assessment: The denial of the map's diminutive characterization remains recognizable, but 'sweet little affair' is an inapplicable English collocation for a physical mountain and obscures 代物's dismissive reference.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that, by any measure, it is not anything so cute or modest.

adjudicated.jp: 地図で見て文字通り丘と勘違いし、ワイフとマイサン引き連れてハイキングになど行こうものなら、家族ぐるみで遭難することうけあいである。
adjudicated.en: Taking the word of the map literally and mistaking them for a hill, someone who's planning a wife-and-my-son hiking trip or something will then be met with a guaranteed family-wide stranding.
comments: See CCC4016, CCX0001. The father taking up religion will involve the family; son against the father, daughter against the mother, brother against brother. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The hypothetical reliance on the map, the comic family-hike phrasing, and the guaranteed family-wide stranding are all present. The English is grammatically rough but does not substitute a different outcome.

adjudicated.jp: 都会との交通手段は、電車と未舗装の山道しかない。
adjudicated.en: Means of transportation in and out of town are a train and an unpaved mountain trail, nothing else.
adjudicated.assessment: The exclusivity of the two transport links—the train and an unpaved mountain road—is preserved. 'Trail' slightly narrows 道 but remains compatible with the described route.

adjudicated.jp: 一応、反対方向の峠まで行けば、道がある。
adjudicated.en: Technically, if you go towards the opposite ridge, there is a road.
comments: Far western road, beyond the bridge. That's where Kiri'll go practice, and parts of CCZAS are there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The qualified alternative of reaching a road by going to the pass in the opposite direction is preserved. 'Ridge' is less exact than 'pass' but does not reverse the route.

adjudicated.jp: ただし本当に遠回りになる。
adjudicated.en: However, in truth you'll just end up detoured.
adjudicated.assessment: The warning that the alternative becomes a substantial detour is preserved, though 'end up detoured' is awkwardly phrased.

adjudicated.jp: それくらい無駄に距離がある。
adjudicated.en: There's little more than a length of pointless distance.
comments: There are two ways out of this town: the train (which doesn't run for him), and the tiiiny little road that passes by the only religious building in the whole world. The alternative is something that looks like a road, but just makes you run in circles. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English signals pointless distance, but 'little more than a length' reverses the scale suggested by それくらい and fails to state that the places are unnecessarily far apart. The intended judgment is recoverable only indirectly.
adjudicated.remedy: State that they are that pointlessly far apart.

adjudicated.jp: 田舎です。
adjudicated.en: 'Tis but countryside.
comments: Randomly formal. See CCZAS, where Taichi lives on the far western side, in the wilderness, because he thinks himself an animal: there is no exit down that road. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The concise identification of the area as countryside is preserved. The mock-archaic contraction is a stylistic addition but does not alter the fact.

adjudicated.jp: 以前、クラスの桜庭という男が、
adjudicated.en: Some time ago, this guy Sakuraba from my class said:
adjudicated.assessment: The earlier occasion, class relationship, and named male student are preserved. Supplying 'said' anticipates the quotation introduced by the Japanese fragment but remains structurally compatible.

adjudicated.jp: 『このＮＥＷチャリで峠を制覇してみせる。これって、今の俺には必要なことだと思うから』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: 『I will prove myself by conquering the peak with this new bike. Because... I think that's what I need to do for my sake, right now.』
comments: This is an extremely important line, considering that he manages to head to the outside world (heaven) with the bike. Which is a tricky vehicle to use in this place, see CCA0004, but is used by Nanaka like it's nothing, see CCA0003. See CCZAS, Mad Taichi (who uses that bike like nobody's business because it's that much of a troll) will also say this line. Notice the NEW in western Kanji(sp): Sakuraba should speak American. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The new bicycle, intended conquest of the pass, and belief that the act is presently necessary are all recoverable. 'Prove myself' and 'for my sake' add motives not stated, while 'peak' narrows 峠 from a mountain pass.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the boast about conquering the pass and its present necessity without the added self-proof motive.

adjudicated.jp: と歯を輝かせながら旅だったことがある。
adjudicated.en: And so he left for his journey, all while his teeth shined.
adjudicated.assessment: The departure, journey framing, and gleaming-teeth image are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: で。
adjudicated.en: Then,
adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt connective that turns to the consequence is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭は丸三日帰宅せず、警察の御出動と相成った。
adjudicated.en: it came that Sakuraba did not return home for three full days, so that the police was formally dispatched.
comments: See CCC3025. Same time! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The three full days without returning home and resulting police deployment are preserved. Singular agreement with 'police' is mechanical.

adjudicated.jp: 買ったばかりのマウンテンバイクを軽く試し乗りしようとしたらしい。
adjudicated.en: He'd sounded like he was trying to take the mountain bike he just bought for a little test ride.
comments: On the useless 'scenery' of the mountain trail of the West, above. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The newly bought mountain bike and intended short test ride are present. らしい marks reported or inferred appearance; 'he'd sounded like' incorrectly implies that the inference came from his speech.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an impersonal 'apparently' rather than attributing a sounding-like statement to him.

adjudicated.jp: が、調子に乗って隣町の相原市（超遠い）へあと五キロという地点にまで到達したところで故障。
adjudicated.en: But, getting carried out in the moment, he had a breakdown after getting to a point about five kilometers from the neighboring town of Aihara City (hyper far away).
comments: Keeping 超 consistent as it seems a bit of a running gag. The bike will take you far, but not everywhere on its own. A "Aihara" seems to exist, dunno the point of it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that after getting carried away and reaching a point five kilometers short of the distant neighboring city, the bicycle broke down. 'He had a breakdown' instead predicates a personal or psychological breakdown of the rider; the preceding 'getting carried out' also fails to express 調子に乗って.
adjudicated.remedy: Make the bicycle the thing that breaks down after he gets carried away and rides that far.

adjudicated.jp: 車通りの少ない峠の道路を敗走途中、現行犯逮捕された。
adjudicated.en: He was midway through his rout, on a mountain road with little traffic, when he was caught in flagrante delicto and taken into custody.
comments: Wonder how many will try to correct that to 'route'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The defeated retreat along a lightly trafficked mountain road and the arrest in the act are preserved. The Latin phrase is marked but semantically apt.

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭の家はクラスメートの桐原と同じくらい金持ちで、親も過保護だ。
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba's family is very overprotective, like the family of the about equally rich classmate Kirihara.
adjudicated.assessment: The source compares the two households' wealth and adds that Sakuraba's parents are overprotective. The English syntax instead makes Kirihara's family the apparent comparison point for overprotectiveness and buries the wealth comparison inside a noun phrase.
adjudicated.remedy: State the wealth comparison first, then separately describe the parents as overprotective.

adjudicated.jp: 西の桜庭、東の桐原と呼ばれる。
adjudicated.en: They get called Sakurabas of the West, and Kiriharas of the East.
adjudicated.assessment: The paired regional epithets are preserved. Plural family-name morphology is natural in English.

adjudicated.jp: 桐原は武士の家系で、その娘も貴族娘っぽい厳格な雰囲気。
adjudicated.en: The Kiriharas are of warrior lineage, and their daughter also has the stern air of the aristocrat's daughter.
comments: Leaving literal because Taichi is the Aristocrat of Love. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The martial lineage and the daughter's strict aristocratic-young-lady air are preserved. 'Warrior' is broader than 'samurai' but not contradictory.

adjudicated.jp: 家族揃って苦虫を噛みつぶしたような顔をしていて、毒舌で、全体的に愛がない。
adjudicated.en: Her relatives to a one have these sour faces as if they were chewing bitterbugs, the abusive language to match, and on the overall they are devoid of love.
comments: Tsundere runs in the family, IOW. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The family-wide sour expressions, sharp tongues, and general lovelessness remain identifiable. Literal 'bitterbugs' obscures the fixed sour-face idiom, while 'abusive language' overstates 毒舌's cutting speech.
adjudicated.remedy: Use the English sour-face idiom and describe their speech as sharp or acerbic.

adjudicated.jp: 通称『ハラキリ』。
adjudicated.en: Common nickname: "Harakiri".
adjudicated.assessment: The common nickname and its punning form are preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭一族は正反対におっとりとした一族で、父親は盲腸の痛みに気づかず死の一歩手前まで旅だったという武勲の持ち主だ。
adjudicated.en: But the Sakuraba family was the complete opposite, a household of placid gentleness. His father had even accomplished the Feat of Arms of having voyaged to the brink of death by ignoring the pain of his appendicitis.
adjudicated.assessment: 気づかず says the father failed to notice the pain, consistent with the family's oblivious placidity. 'Ignoring' instead implies conscious awareness followed by deliberate disregard and therefore changes the comic causal premise.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he never noticed the appendicitis pain until he was near death.

highlights.text: ignoring the pain of his appendicitis

adjudicated.jp: その天然冒険魂は、確かに息子に継承されていたわけで。
adjudicated.en: That spontaneously adventurous spirit would certainly see a worthy successor in his son.
adjudicated.assessment: The inherited, naturally oblivious adventurous spirit and father-to-son relation are preserved, though 'spontaneously' is less pointed than 天然.

adjudicated.jp: 夜中になっても帰宅しない息子を案じて『誘拐されたんです！』と警察に駆け込むあたり、桜庭一族のまろやかな天然さが垣間見えて面白い。
adjudicated.en: It was funny to see a chink in the Sakurabas' naturally mellow nature when, in the dead of night, said son still had not returned and they anxiously stampeded off to the police shouting "he has been kidnapped!".
adjudicated.assessment: The family's panicked report provides an amusing glimpse of their mellow, guileless obliviousness. Calling it a 'chink in' that nature makes the behavior an exception or breach in the trait rather than an instance that reveals it.
adjudicated.remedy: Present the police report as an amusing glimpse of the family's mellow cluelessness.

highlights.text: a chink in the Sakurabas' naturally mellow nature

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭は関係者に滅茶苦茶叱られ、自転車は没収された。
adjudicated.en: The authorities reprimanded Sakuraba to the fullest, and his bicycle was impounded.
comments: As a Gunjou student attempting escape from the open-air prison, he was lucky. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The severe scolding and bicycle confiscation are preserved. 関係者 means the people concerned or involved; 'the authorities' narrows their identity without support from this line.
adjudicated.remedy: Attribute the reprimand to those involved unless context independently identifies authorities.

adjudicated.jp: くわえて学校中の笑い者となった。
adjudicated.en: And what's more, he became the laughingstock of the school.
adjudicated.assessment: The additional consequence of becoming the whole school's laughingstock is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 校内新聞一面の座を永らく独占し続けもした。
adjudicated.en: He kept monopolizing the top spot of the front page of the school newspaper for a long time.
adjudicated.assessment: His prolonged monopoly of the school newspaper's front page is preserved. 'Top spot of the front page' is redundant but not factually different.

adjudicated.jp: 特にインタビューで奴が口走った内容が受けに受けた。
adjudicated.en: Particularly, the specifics of what he said as he let his mouth run off during the interview made the rounds all around.
comments: Interview was not necessarily on the subject of his escape. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The interview remarks and their exceptional reception remain recognizable, but 受けに受けた means that they were a tremendous hit. 'Made the rounds all around' instead emphasizes circulation and is also idiomatically malformed.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that what he blurted out in the interview was an enormous hit.

adjudicated.jp: 『緊急特報！　蓮ヶ丈奥地に謎の人工建造物を見た！』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: 『Urgent newsflash! In the deep lands of Hasugatake, a mysterious man-made structure was sighted!』
comments: Hasugatake ("The Lotus' Magnificence") is similar to Hasugaike http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%93%AE%E3%83%B6%E6%B1%A0%E9%A7%85, and nothing else returns. Place is straight in the middle of Miyazaki City in the Miyazaki prefecture, ergo it would be a... Miyazaki reference *badum-tish* -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The urgent-news register, remote location, and sighting of a mysterious artificial structure are preserved. Passive voice does not change the reported discovery.

adjudicated.jp: 『完全踏破１２時間、秘境の奥地に隠された禁断のオーバーテクノロジー！！』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: 『A full 12 hours of on-foot travel away, the most secluded backwood region is concealing Forbidden Supertechnology!』
comments: 12 hours both ways? Unclear. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The twelve-hour traversal, remote unexplored depths, hidden object, and forbidden super-technology are all present. 'On-foot' is more specific than 踏破 and may conflict with the surrounding bicycle account; the normalized binding is retained because the source match was not byte-exact.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the route as a twelve-hour traversal without specifying travel mode unless independently established.

adjudicated.jp: 『長い道のりの果て、ここで我々はいまだかつて想像だにしなかった衝撃の事実を見ることになる！』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: 『And at end of this long voyage, we can there finally see a truth so shocking that its impact could never even be imagined!』
comments: This whole thing makes waaay more sense if read metaphorically: the Supertechnology/nuclear power plant is what makes the world rich; in a sense, it's a gift/manifestation of God itself. The Alien is God, and the truth so shocking is, well, Cross Channel is a Christian story, and it has nothing to do with sci-fi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The long journey, climactic location, collective discovery, and unprecedented shocking fact are preserved despite defective articles and word order.

adjudicated.jp: 無茶苦茶だ。
adjudicated.en: Total nonsense.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's blunt dismissal as nonsense is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 要するに奴は、帰宅の途中、道を外れて山に入ったわけだ。
adjudicated.en: In short, this idiot, while coming back home, drifted into a mountain that's not connected with the road.
comments: Map seems to fit, he just walked home on the south side and overshot the area of his mansion, ending towards the power plant. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 道を外れて says that he left or strayed from the road and entered the mountain. The English instead describes the mountain itself as unconnected to the road, relocating the relation and adding a geographic claim absent from the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he strayed off the road and into the mountain on his way home.

highlights.text: drifted into a mountain that's not connected with the road

adjudicated.jp: おそらく近道目的だったんだろう。
adjudicated.en: He probably wanted to try a shortcut.
adjudicated.assessment: The tentative inference that he intended a shortcut is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: そして偶然、とある施設を発見して大興奮した。
adjudicated.en: And then, he accidentally discovered a certain facility, and became all excited.
adjudicated.assessment: The chance discovery of a certain facility and ensuing excitement are preserved. 'Accidentally' is slightly less neutral than 'by chance' but remains compatible.

adjudicated.jp: インタビューはこの後も、凄まじい展開となった。
adjudicated.en: After this, the interview became even more absurd:
adjudicated.assessment: The interview's escalation into an extraordinary development is preserved. 'Absurd' selects a comic evaluation supported by the immediately preceding dismissal.

adjudicated.jp: 『秘密基地が』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: "In the hidden base..."
adjudicated.assessment: The quoted fragment marks 'the secret base' with が as its grammatical subject. The English converts it into a location introduced by 'in,' and replaces the compound's conventional 'secret base' sense with 'hidden base.'
adjudicated.remedy: Keep 'the secret base' as the suspended subject of the quoted fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 『衝撃の』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: "...shocking..."
adjudicated.assessment: The suspended attributive fragment conveys the same shocking or impact-related force without supplying a new object.

adjudicated.jp: 『武装した兵隊らによって』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: "...because of armed soldiers..."
adjudicated.assessment: The armed soldiers remain present, but によって most directly marks agency or means in this fragment. 'Because of' recasts that grammatical relation as undifferentiated cause, so the intended attachment remains only approximately recoverable.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the suspended agentive phrase as 'by armed soldiers.'

adjudicated.jp: 『人類の常識を覆す』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: "...the defiance of the conventional wisdom of humanity!"
comments: In one: 秘密基地が衝撃の武装した兵隊らによって人類の常識を覆す or "Humanity's conventional wisdom will be defied by the shocking presence of armed soldiers in the hidden base!" Still unsure if these are supposed to flow into each other. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment's idea of overturning humanity's conventional wisdom is preserved through the nominalized 'defiance' phrasing.

adjudicated.jp: 本インタビューで使用された単語ベスト５。
adjudicated.en: These are the top five words, by frequency, in the interview:
comments: Super Memory is possibly what lets him remember this absurdly irrelevant trivia... except why would he remember irrelevant trivia about one of the more annoying guys he knows? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The top-five words used in the interview are identified correctly. The following ranked counts make the added 'by frequency' explicit rather than speculative.

adjudicated.jp: 校内新聞は、桜庭という美味なる獲物を骨の髄までしゃぶり尽くした。
adjudicated.en: The campus newspaper suckled on the bones of the delicious game named Sakuraba until there was nothing left.
adjudicated.assessment: The school newspaper, Sakuraba as delectable prey, and exploitation down to the marrow are all preserved. 'Suckled on the bones' uses the nursing verb rather than sucking or gnawing something clean and produces a materially different English image.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the prey metaphor and say the paper sucked or picked him clean to the marrow.

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭は報道の残酷さを思い知った。
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba understood with his flesh the cruelty of the press.
adjudicated.assessment: 思い知った means that he learned or came to understand the cruelty of the press, generally through harsh experience. The source has no body or flesh expression; adding one turns the idiom into an unsupported physical image.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he learned the cruelty of the press the hard way.

adjudicated.jp: その後、ストレスで腹を下して一週間ほど下痢をした（記事になった）。
adjudicated.en: Afterwards, his bowels loosened via stress and he had diarrhea for a week (this became an article).
adjudicated.assessment: The stress-induced digestive illness, approximate one-week duration, and its becoming an article are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 八日目の朝にはけろっとした顔で登校してきた（取材された）。
adjudicated.en: On the morning of the eighth day, he attended school with nonchalance on his face (inquiries on this were made by the paper)...
comments: 7 days to recover, and on the 8 he returns... different. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The eighth morning, unconcerned appearance, return to school, and follow-up reporting are preserved. The parenthetical elaborates the implied newspaper context but does not change the event.

adjudicated.jp: 髪を金髪に染めて（特集記事・異論反論オブジェクションのネタになった）。
adjudicated.en: ...and his hair dyed the color of gold (they became material for a special report with man on the street pros-and-cons interviews).
comments: Connected to the above, the article is the same in both sentences. http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%AD%91%E7%B4%AB%E5%93%B2%E4%B9%9F_NEWS23#.E7.95.B0.E8.AB.96.21.E5.8F.8D.E8.AB.96.21OBJECTION seems to be what is meant -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Dyeing the hair blond and becoming material for a feature are present. The English turns the title-like phrase into a specific format of street interviews, leaves the hair without a clear actor, and uses a plural pronoun for the singular hair change.
adjudicated.remedy: State that he dyed his hair blond and that it became material for the named or quoted feature.

adjudicated.jp: 以来、奴はずっと金髪ライフ。
adjudicated.en: Ever since then, the guy's lived the blond life.
adjudicated.assessment: The colloquial observation that he has lived the blond-haired life ever since is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: きっと、新しい自分になる、という錯覚を己に課すことでストレスを克服したんだろう。
adjudicated.en: He overcame the stress by imposing his self with the deluded belief that he'd become anew, definitely.
adjudicated.assessment: The self-imposed illusion of becoming a new self and the inferred conquest of stress are preserved. The sentence-final 'definitely' misplaces きっと, which supports the narrator's probable inference together with だろう, and 'imposing his self' is defective English.
adjudicated.remedy: Frame the whole explanation as the narrator's probability and describe imposing the illusion on himself.

adjudicated.jp: ……これが元で金銀コンビなどと称されることになったわけだが。
adjudicated.en: ...however, that's also how we came to be known as the Gold-Silver Pair.
comments: Word typically used for Miki and Kiri. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The causal transition and resulting Gold-Silver Pair label are preserved, including the trailing qualification.

adjudicated.jp: 閑話休題。
adjudicated.en: But I digress.
adjudicated.assessment: The standard return-from-digression function is rendered with an appropriate English idiom.

adjudicated.jp: もちろん桜庭が見た外宇宙から来訪した超知的生命体が極秘裏に建築した施設というのは原子力発電所なわけだが、これは市民に豊潤なる富をもたらした。
adjudicated.en: Of course the structure built in great secrecy on the other side of the mountains by hyper intelligent beings visiting us from deep space that Sakuraba saw was in fact a nuclear power plant, which had brought about the abundant wealth of the locals.
comments: 豊 = Yutaka's name. Will recur in unexpected places. Of course a significant part of the subtext. Curiously, there's also another structure built in apparent secrecy by ultraintelligent being(s) possibly visiting from off the world in this mountain... one way more important than the power plant. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock extraterrestrial builders, secret construction, actual nuclear plant, and resulting civic wealth are preserved. 'On the other side of the mountains' is inserted into the structure's location even though this source sentence does not state that relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the intentionally elaborate identification without adding a location clause.

adjudicated.jp: 二束三文の土地が、みるみるうちに札束に変わった。
adjudicated.en: In the strike of the blink of an eye, this three pennies for two acres of a land was transformed into rolls of banknotes.
comments: There's a two and there's a three... grrr, where's the other two? Maybe that miru-miru. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 二束三文 is an idiom meaning virtually worthless or dirt-cheap, not a literal price-to-acre conversion. The English invents pennies and acreage, while みるみるうち means visibly or rapidly rather than 'in the strike of the blink.'
adjudicated.remedy: Say that dirt-cheap land rapidly turned into bundles of cash.

highlights.text: this three pennies for two acres of a land

adjudicated.jp: 近代化が進み、文明が開化した。
adjudicated.en: Modernization progressed, culture got civilized.
comments: This sounds just as ridiculous in the original. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The advance of modernization and flourishing of civilization remain recognizable. 'Culture got civilized' changes 文明 to culture and produces a tautological, unnatural relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep modernization advancing and civilization flourishing or opening up.

adjudicated.jp: 富豪が何人も誕生し、ビルが建ち、人が増えた。
adjudicated.en: With everybody reborn a millionaire, buildings were constructed, and people increased.
comments: I don't get it, shouldn't it be "tents were erected, and people were constructed"? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 何人も says that a number of wealthy people or tycoons emerged. The English changes this limited group into everybody and adds literal rebirth, substantially exaggerating the distribution of wealth.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that several fortunes or wealthy magnates emerged as buildings and population increased.

adjudicated.jp: 土地は安く、税金も安い。
adjudicated.en: The land is cheap, the taxes just as cheap.
adjudicated.assessment: Both cheap land and cheap taxes are preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 電気代はタダだ。
adjudicated.en: Electricity is free of charge.
adjudicated.assessment: The absence of electricity charges is preserved exactly.

adjudicated.jp: だから街には無意味な照明が無数にある。
adjudicated.en: Therefore, there are so many useless lighting fixtures throughout town.
comments: These may be what illuminate the forest where Kiri practices to day-level. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The causal relation and profusion of pointless lighting throughout town are preserved. 'So many' is less absolute than 無数 but remains within the intended hyperbole.

adjudicated.jp: だからといって、ベンチにライトを仕込むことはないだろうに。
adjudicated.en: Nevertheless, they didn't 'rearn' to build the benches 'light', didn't they.
comments: grrrrroooooaaaaannnnn ライト = light + right, 仕込む = build into + teach/learn. I suppose it's harder to spot in Japanese. Perhaps a warning that even the Japanese better know enough English to spot this stuff if they want to understand some of the jokes and themes. Works backwards still: better know just a pinch of Japanese, or you'll be losing some of this stuff regardless. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ‘Rearn’ and ‘light’ deliberately recreate both source pivots: 仕込む as install/train and ライト as light/right. GHS’s attached note identifies the same mechanism. The result is tortured English, but it is a functioning two-part replacement pun rather than an accidental reversal of the source.
adjudicated.remedy: If revising, retain both overlapping puns in a clearer complaint.

adjudicated.jp: 市はそのテーマを『癒し』と定めた。
adjudicated.en: The township decided that its theme would be 'healing'.
comments: See Gunjou. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The municipal decision and 'healing' theme are preserved. 'Township' is a marked and jurisdictionally narrower term for 市 in the established city context.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'city' or 'municipality' consistently.

adjudicated.jp: 原子力発電所などというものを抱えている僻地が、いかにも掲げそうなお題目である。
adjudicated.en: For a remote place with a nuclear plant nearby, that's a very empty slogan to hoist up.
adjudicated.assessment: The remote place, its nuclear plant, and the pointedly apt slogan are preserved. Calling お題目 an empty slogan is contextually defensible.

adjudicated.jp: 市役所に至ってはロココ様式のそれはもう耽美的な建物で、外観から内装に至るまで『汝を癒してやろう』という厳かな気概に溢れ、来庁者を萎縮させまくっている。
adjudicated.en: The city hall building itself was an extremely aesthetic building in Rococo style, that overflows from the exterior all the way to the interior with the stately fighting spirit of "How Thou Shall Be Healed!", so as to overwhelm anyone visiting there on official business.
comments: Highly sarcastic. Town hall seems to be in this side, but it's not on the map, never seen, and only one other time ever mentioned. Supposing it's in the south side, east of the Sakuraba mansion. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rococo city hall, aesthetic excess, healing proclamation, and intimidation of visitors are present. 'Fighting spirit' is over-literal for solemn 気概, 'How Thou Shall Be Healed' is defective and changes a direct promise into a malformed exclamation, and 'so as to overwhelm' turns the effect into purpose.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the solemn 'We shall heal thee' spirit as the quality whose excess intimidates visitors.

adjudicated.jp: ちぐはぐな土地。
adjudicated.en: What an incongruous land.
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment's judgment of the place as mismatched or incongruous is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: だから……居心地が良いのかもしれないな。
adjudicated.en: Therefore... living here might just be very comfortable.
adjudicated.assessment: The tentative conclusion that this may be why the place feels comfortable is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 壊れてしまった世界は、妙に親近感を抱かせる。
adjudicated.en: A world split and broken that inspires an odd affinity in me.
adjudicated.assessment: The broken world and the odd sense of affinity it inspires are preserved. The English remains a sentence fragment but retains the relation.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent dialogue beat is preserved. The source string is highly duplicated, but this occurrence is uniquely bracketed by the resolved preceding and following records in the same authoritative script.

adjudicated.jp: 「いて」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ow."
adjudicated.assessment: The clipped pain interjection is preserved with a natural English equivalent.

adjudicated.jp: 軽薄な音がした。
adjudicated.en: A frivolous sound emitted,
comments: Odd term. I suppose since this may actually not even happen at all... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The occurrence of a light, frivolous sound is preserved, though 'emitted' leaves its source syntactically unstated.

adjudicated.jp: 頭がかくんと傾く。
adjudicated.en: my head sunk forwards with a thunk,
adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt movement of the head is recognizable, but 'sunk forwards' adds direction, 'with a thunk' converts the movement mimetic into an audible impact, and the present event becomes past tense.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the head suddenly tilting or jerking without an added impact sound.

adjudicated.jp: 首筋の筋がひきつって、ものすごく痛い。
adjudicated.en: and the muscles of my nape stiffened with indescribable pain.
adjudicated.assessment: The neck muscles and intense pain are present, but ひきつって indicates twitching or cramping rather than merely stiffening, and ものすごく means extremely rather than indescribably.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that the neck muscles cramp or seize with tremendous pain.

adjudicated.jp: 「……なんだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...the hell."
adjudicated.assessment: The irritated, suspended 'what is it' reaction is conveyed by the colloquial English fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 振り向けば、そこに少女が一人。
adjudicated.en: If I look over my shoulder, there stands, alone, a girl.
comments: Apparent ability to stand alone is what got Taichi into Touko, important. That "if"... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The turn, solitary girl, and her location are preserved. The narrative discovery becomes a present-tense conditional—'If I look'—rather than the source's contextual 'when I turned/looked around,' leaving the event grammatically unstable.
adjudicated.remedy: Render the turn and discovery as the narrative event occurring in context.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんだ、女帝か」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "My, it is the Empress!"
adjudicated.assessment: The recognition and teasing imperial epithet are preserved. 'My' is a light register embellishment rather than a different proposition.

adjudicated.en: Girl: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is preserved. Its duplicated source string is bound to the unique candidate bracketed by the resolved preceding and following records in the same authoritative script.

adjudicated.jp: 「女王陛下にはご機嫌うるわしゅう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The most pleasant wishes that this meeting finds You in good health, Your Majesty."
comments: Mocking high register. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-courtly wish for Her Majesty's good health is preserved, though expanded into ceremonially elaborate English.

adjudicated.jp: 片手をあげて挨拶する。
adjudicated.en: A greeting with one raised hand.
comments: HEIL TOUKHITLER!!1 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The raised hand and greeting action are preserved. The English nominalizes the action into a fragment but does not change it.

adjudicated.en: Girl: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The second silent response is preserved and is independently topology-bound to the sole duplicate candidate between its resolved same-script neighbors.

adjudicated.jp: エスプリのきいた言葉には、ウィットに富んだ返しがあってしかるべきなのだ。
adjudicated.en: To those words so rich in esprit, a retort wealthy in wit would be suitable.
comments: Accents don't work, likely Shift-JIS. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The expectation that esprit-rich words deserve a witty reply is preserved. Repeating the wealth metaphor is awkward but source-compatible.

adjudicated.jp: そんなような。
adjudicated.en: Like...
comments: swapped around
adjudicated.assessment: そんなような closes the imagined example as 'something like that.' The English leaves only 'Like...' and drops the demonstrative content, making the connection less recoverable.
adjudicated.remedy: Close the example with 'Something like that.'

adjudicated.jp: 『くわ～っ、誰が女帝か～っ、馬鹿言ってんじゃないですわ、すわすわっ！！』
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Gwaaa～h, whooo are you calling an Empreee～ss! You shan't say something so stupid, shan't shan't!!!"
comments: This needs to read like it walked out of some bad overwrought moege, sort of like this route really. ～ for further cliched silliness. Shan't, see CCD0008B -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The imagined protest, rejection of the epithet, accusation of nonsense, and exaggerated speech-tic parody are all functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: だが期待したような返答はない。
adjudicated.en: But there's no reply of the type expected.
comments: From a Tsundere. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The absence of the expected kind of reply is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: それどころか冷然とした怒気さえ感じられた。
adjudicated.en: On the contrary, all I could feel was her cold-hearted wrath.
adjudicated.assessment: The cool anger felt instead of a reply is present. さえ means even an air of anger could be felt, not that wrath was all the narrator could feel; 'cold-hearted' also attributes character rather than the source's cold or composed quality.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that, if anything, even a chill air of anger could be felt.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうしたの、桐原。ノリ悪いよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What's the problem, Kirihara? You're not getting into the spirit here."
adjudicated.assessment: The question and complaint that the addressee is not playing along are preserved with a natural English idiom.

adjudicated.jp: 「もしかしてアレ？　生理っぽいやつ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Could it be that thing? That biological-ish thing?"
adjudicated.assessment: 生理 in this teasing context specifically refers to menstruation or a period. 'Biological-ish thing' removes the referent almost entirely and turns a pointedly intrusive question into a vague abstraction.
adjudicated.remedy: Retain the euphemistic but unmistakable reference to a period.

adjudicated.assessment: The extended silence is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 空気がどんどん重くなってく。
adjudicated.en: The mood grows steadily heaver,
adjudicated.assessment: The steadily worsening heaviness of the atmosphere is preserved. 'Heaver' is a typographic error for 'heavier.'

adjudicated.jp: でも止まらない。
adjudicated.en: but I don't stop.
comments: Minor emphasis on how he doesn't necessarily wish to go on. There'll be relatively few explicit hints of this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The continuation despite the worsening atmosphere is preserved. Supplying the narrator as subject is contextually supported.

adjudicated.jp: 「月桂冠」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wreath of laurel."
adjudicated.assessment: The literal lexical sense of 月桂冠 is a laurel crown or wreath, but the form is also a proper-name and wordplay-bearing expression in Japanese. Selecting only the literal object may discard the intended association in this sequence.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the expression as a proper name or annotate the literal laurel-crown sense if the surrounding wordplay requires both.

adjudicated.jp: 「黒須太一……」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Kurosu Taichi...!"
adjudicated.assessment: The name and trailing pause are preserved, but the English adds an exclamation mark that changes the restrained ellipsis into an overt outburst.
adjudicated.remedy: Retain the name followed only by the suspended pause.

adjudicated.jp: 怒りの波動が膨れあがる。
adjudicated.en: The wave of rage swells up and outwards.
adjudicated.assessment: The swelling wave or aura of anger is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「赤飯」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Auspicious red rice."
adjudicated.assessment: The red-rice item is preserved, with its auspicious cultural association made explicit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子……桐原の下の名前、内心ではバリバリ呼び捨て……の額のあたりがひきつった。
adjudicated.en: Touko... that's Kirihara's first name, and in my mind I vigorously strip it of honorifics... began to have a contraction in the dead center of her forehead.
adjudicated.assessment: The first-name aside, private use without an honorific, and forehead twitch are all present. 'Strip it of honorifics' makes 呼び捨て mechanically literal, 'vigorously' misplaces バリバリ's emphatic slang, and 'dead center' over-specifies 額のあたり.
adjudicated.remedy: Use natural English for privately calling her by her bare first name, then describe a twitch around her forehead.

adjudicated.jp: 「のぉっ！」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "'llyyy!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a clipped tail that the next line reconstructs as こんのぉっ. The English fragment follows its own reconstruction of 'really,' which is not the natural value of the Japanese insult-like 'you...!' form.
adjudicated.remedy: Coordinate the clipped syllable with a reconstruction equivalent to an angry 'you...!'

adjudicated.jp: 実際には『こんのぉっ！』と言ってる。
adjudicated.en: In truth, she's saying "reallyyy!",
adjudicated.assessment: こんのぉっ is an angry, drawn-out この, roughly an incomplete 'you...!' or 'you little...!' It does not mean 'really.' The reconstruction therefore substitutes a different word and breaks the explanation of the clipped preceding cry.
adjudicated.remedy: Reconstruct the cry as a lisped or clipped angry 'you...!' expression.

adjudicated.jp: 舌ったらずなのだろう。
adjudicated.en: so that had to have been her lisp.
adjudicated.assessment: The tentative attribution to immature or indistinct articulation is conveyed by 'lisp,' though the English phrasing is awkward.

adjudicated.jp: 彼女の特徴的イントネーションだ。
adjudicated.en: It's her characteristic intonation.
adjudicated.assessment: The characteristic intonation is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 令嬢然とした冬子が、口調に未熟さを残しているのは、正直笑えた。
adjudicated.en: It honestly made me laugh how Touko, so like a proper lady, still had immaturity in speech remaining inside her.
comments: General returning concept, she still has something of the infant in her for starters - see CCB2101 for more uhmmm infantile things she does with the mouth (sucking cock while sleeping). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The contrast between a proper young-lady bearing and lingering immaturity of speech, together with the narrator's amusement, is preserved despite stiff English.

adjudicated.jp: と。
adjudicated.en: And,
adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt connective into the interruption is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ごっ
adjudicated.en: Smack!
adjudicated.assessment: The blunt impact sound is represented with a conventional English effect.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...g'fuh?!"
adjudicated.assessment: The startled impact grunt and punctuation are preserved functionally.

adjudicated.jp: チンだった。
adjudicated.en: It was on my chin.
comments: or on his dick. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The chin as the point of impact is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: クリーンヒットだった。
adjudicated.en: It was a clean hit.
adjudicated.assessment: The clean-hit judgment is preserved exactly.

adjudicated.jp: 避ける暇もなかった。
adjudicated.en: It was too fast to dodge.
adjudicated.assessment: The absence of any opportunity to dodge is preserved through the natural implication that the blow was too fast to evade.

adjudicated.jp: 拳に突き上げられ、のけぞるように顎先が天をさす。
adjudicated.en: Thrust upwards by the fist, the tip of my chin points to the heavens, the head thrown backwards.
adjudicated.assessment: The upward force of the fist, backward recoil, and chin pointing skyward are all retained despite a syntactically crowded English sentence.

adjudicated.jp: ゲームっぽい架空エフェクトが、脳裏に踊る。
adjudicated.en: A videogame-like Imaginary special effect danced in my mind.
comments: It's actually "Air-" as in air-friends and air-guitars. There'll be a fair few of these, and they seem to indicate Taichi's memory leak of videogames into reality. Notice this very first one followed right after being beaten. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The game-like imaginary effect dancing through the narrator's mind is preserved directly; the capitalization is merely eccentric.

adjudicated.jp: 「……撤収手伝いなさいよ」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "...now come help take down the tents."
comments: The death of Tentman. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The order to help dismantle and pack up is preserved; specifying the tents is supported by the immediate campsite context.

adjudicated.jp: 低い声だ。
adjudicated.en: It's a low voice.
adjudicated.assessment: The low voice is preserved exactly.

adjudicated.jp: これ以上ごねるなら今度は空じゃなくて地面にＫＩＳＳすることになるぜ。
adjudicated.en: If you fuss anymore from now, next time it won't be the sky that you implement a kiss with, but the ground.
adjudicated.assessment: The warning that further resistance will make him kiss the ground rather than the sky is fully recoverable. The English collocation is extremely awkward but does not alter the proposition.

adjudicated.jp: 暗にそう申しておられた。
adjudicated.en: That was the interwoven implication.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's mock-deferential observation that this was being said implicitly is preserved, though 'interwoven' is an unnecessary flourish.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい、テツダイマス（ガクガク）」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yes ma'am, help I shall! (clatter, clatter)"
comments: Of teeth. These odd emoticon-like things seem less odd, perhaps, if reread straight from CCX0001. They'll be gone pretty quickly, however. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The frightened compliance is retained, but ガクガク conventionally depicts violent trembling. 'Clatter, clatter' narrows it to an inferred sound, apparently teeth, that the source does not specify.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a parenthetical stage effect such as '(tremble, tremble)' or otherwise preserve whole-body shaking.

adjudicated.jp: 無言で俺の耳を引いてキャンプ場に向かう。
adjudicated.en: Without a word, my ear gets pulled as we head towards the camping ground.
adjudicated.assessment: The silent ear-pulling and movement toward the campsite are preserved. The passive construction is stiff but contextually identifies the action.

adjudicated.jp: 「あっ、あっ、いたいですーっ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ow, ow, that huuurts!"
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated cry and drawn-out complaint of pain are preserved functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 「殴った私の手も痛いわ」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "The hand I hit you with also hurts!"
adjudicated.assessment: The retort that the striking hand also hurts is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「男手少ないんだから、キリキリ働きなさいよ」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "We have so few men helping, so chop chop and get to work now!"
comments: Kiri Kiri. Her name'll also pop up. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 'Chop chop' naturally conveys キリキリ as an order to work briskly, but it removes the audible repetition of the addressee's name embedded in キリキリ. That secondary echo is locally salient enough to warrant preservation if possible.
adjudicated.remedy: Use brisk wording that can retain or recreate the repeated name-sound without obscuring the command.

adjudicated.jp: 「働いたじゃないか、合宿中にたくさん……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But I worked, didn't I, throughout camp and lots..."
adjudicated.assessment: The protest that he already worked a great deal during camp is preserved, despite unnatural placement of 'lots.'

adjudicated.jp: 「最後まで気を抜かないの」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Don't relax until the last moment, you!"
adjudicated.assessment: The instruction not to relax or let one's guard down until the end is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「……ちょっとの休息も許されない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...not even allowed a short break."
comments: Significantly less funny considering how horrible it is for him to be here. No wonder he shatters into Another Story. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The complaint that even a brief rest is not permitted is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は戦士か。
adjudicated.en: What am I, a soldier?
comments: See CCA0027. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 戦士 can legitimately be soldier, warrior, or fighter. No distinct terminology callback is established here, so the audit's categorical distinction is unsupported.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic or grammatical revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: 「桐原」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Kirihara."
adjudicated.assessment: The surname address is preserved exactly and bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.en: Touko: "...what?"
comments: Oddly flat, considering. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The suspended, flat question is preserved directly and bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「合宿、来てよかったろ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You're glad you came to training camp, right?"
adjudicated.assessment: The leading question that coming to camp was worthwhile is preserved naturally.
The extended silence is preserved and bound to the canonical occurrence selected by sequence resolution.

adjudicated.jp: 「（ぷいっ）」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "(Pfui.)"
comments: This may be the first instance of use of this term since the year 1952. Caren't. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ぷいっ conventionally stages a huffy turn away. 'Pfui' supplies an audible expression of disgust instead, retaining the attitude but changing the action into speech-like sound.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a parenthetical huff-and-turn stage effect rather than a spoken interjection.

adjudicated.jp: 無視された。
adjudicated.en: I was ignored.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's observation that he was ignored is preserved exactly.

adjudicated.jp: 会話はずまないことけたたましい。
adjudicated.en: A clamorously wild failure to enliven the conversation.
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately noisy hyperbole for a conversation spectacularly failing to get going is preserved, though the English fragment is strained.

adjudicated.jp: これでも今日は滅茶苦茶話している方だ。
adjudicated.en: And for all this, today's the day to speak out nonsense wantonly.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that even this counts as talking an extraordinary amount today, relative to their norm. The English instead makes today an occasion for speaking nonsense recklessly, misreading 滅茶苦茶 as the content or manner of speech and losing the comparative 話している方だ construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that, even so, they have talked an extraordinary amount today by their usual standard.

highlights.text: today's the day to speak out nonsense wantonly.

adjudicated.jp: 今日みたいにかけあい漫才をすることの方が、むしろ珍しい。
adjudicated.en: It's rather rare to have days of comedic duets like today.
comments: Very odd pair. I suppose this is a warning that he's going to hallucinate the rest to avoid going insane. This next dialogue, I believe, doesn't happen at all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rarity of their doing a comic back-and-forth like today's is preserved. 'Comedic duet' is broad but supported.

adjudicated.jp: 「軽いあたま」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Empty-head."
comments: So odd she'd try to play along despite it all, isn't it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The insult is recoverable, but 軽い is 'light' or 'shallow,' not 'empty.' Replacing it with 'empty' collapses the setup into the following hollow-sound explanation and loses the source's shift from lightness to emptiness.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve 'light head' or another formulation that leaves the subsequent hollow/empty explanation as a separate turn.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What?"
adjudicated.assessment: The questioning response is naturally rendered as 'What?' and bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「殴ったとき、空っぽの音がしたから」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "When I punched you, it sounded hollow."
adjudicated.assessment: The explanation that the punch produced a hollow or empty sound is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「そろそろ脳細胞、分裂させておかないと、大人になった時につらいわよ？」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "If you don't let your neurons undergo division but quick, it'll be harsh when you reach adulthood, you know?"
comments: Neurons do not undergo cell division. Well, there seems to be some controversial experiments hinting they do regenerate within limits, but the only way brain cells would be splitting is if Taichi were not yet born, not a moron. Touko may be making a reaaally bad joke about splitting neurons, which would still leave the issue of how to fill an empty head except with neurons undergoing mitosis, but the joke would be flatter than Miki's reset chest.

Most importantly, it's out of tone for her. OTOH, if taken literally, it is consistent with the absolute pile of bullcrap that'll be seen all throughout Cross Channel, most importantly in the ending - see CCX0001. This is the clue that Taichi could be hallucinating at least this part, it being his usual pretentious and ignorant verbiage, as well as the first sign that those who don't have a clue about scientific stuff are about to get creamed... and not because they won't understand it.
This is fairly evident as far as scientific trolls go: brain cells not undergoing mitosis is well known. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mocking warning to get the brain cells dividing before adulthood is preserved. 'But quick' is awkward but carries the urgency.

adjudicated.jp: 「失敬だな。弁護士は通っとるのか？　ああん？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, how rude! Do we gotta go by lawyers now? Well?"
comments: This should remind of an arguing couple trying for divorce. Not the first time he'll bring up their old story in a manner this almost outrageously obnoxious, so it's intended to sound very different on second reading. This may be his answer to her 'pfui'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The offended, confrontational tone and lawyer reference survive, but 'Do we gotta go by lawyers now?' does not clearly express the source's question about whether the remark or matter has been put through or cleared by a lawyer.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a confrontational question equivalent to 'Did you clear that with your lawyer?' while retaining the rough tone.

adjudicated.jp: 「ほんっと……疲れる……きみ……」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "...you are... really... tiresome..."
comments: This might be real. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The halting complaint that the addressee is truly exhausting is preserved naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 盛大にため息をつかれると、こちらも萎える。
adjudicated.en: With a lengthy, exasperated sigh, this also withers.
adjudicated.assessment: こちらも refers back to the narrator: being met with such an extravagant sigh makes him lose heart or wilt as well. 'This also withers' replaces the person with an unanchored demonstrative and fails to identify whose spirits fall.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that the grand sigh makes the narrator wilt or lose heart too.

adjudicated.jp: 黙って連行される。
adjudicated.en: I'm escorted in silence.
adjudicated.assessment: Being silently led or hauled away is preserved by 'escorted in silence.'

adjudicated.jp: 視線はついつい、高そうなワンピースをしっとりとまとわりつかせた臀部に。
adjudicated.en: Against my better judgment, my sight runs down her of expensive-looking one-piece dress coiling down to her rear.
comments: Let's go with ambiguous. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The involuntary gaze, expensive-looking dress, and rear remain identifiable, but the broken syntax obscures that the dress clings sleekly or sensuously around the buttocks rather than merely coiling downward toward them.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe his gaze drifting despite himself to the buttocks hugged by the expensive-looking dress.

adjudicated.jp: 「水蜜桃」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "White peach."
adjudicated.assessment: The juicy white-peach image is preserved with a recognized English name for the fruit.

adjudicated.jp: 聞こえないようつぶやく。
adjudicated.en: I mutter as not to be heard.
adjudicated.assessment: Muttering so as not to be heard is preserved despite the missing 'so' in the English construction.

adjudicated.jp: 「触ったら沈めるから」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Touch it and I sink you."
comments: Excellent hearing... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The threat to sink or put him under if he touches is preserved tersely.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silence is preserved. Its heavily duplicated source string is bound to the unique same-script candidate strictly bracketed by the resolved preceding and following records.

adjudicated.jp: ど、どこに？（ブルブル）
adjudicated.en: I-into what? (shudder, shudder)
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered question and trembling are preserved. 'Into what?' is contextually licensed by the preceding threat to sink him.

adjudicated.jp: 「せっかく夏期休暇、一週間無駄にした気分よ」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "It was my precious Summer Vacation, and now it feels like I wasted a whole week of it!"
comments: This seems to make a liiittle more sense than the above. Touko would want to be away from Gunjou for Summer. So why wasn't she on the other side of the world or something...? Sakuraba I can understand, but Touko? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The feeling of having wasted a precious full week of summer vacation is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「意訳すると、楽しい合宿も終わりかにゃー、って感じだな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "To paraphrase, 'this fun training camp is comeowing to an ennnd!', that's what it feels, right."
comments: "Little did they know that the nyans were only the beginning..." from The Chronicles of How an Innocent-Looking Translation Destroyed the World. Slightly more relevantly, this is Taichi intentionally misunderstanding. One of the few rare moments in which this is explicit. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The overt loose paraphrase, regret at the fun camp ending, and catlike にゃ wordplay are all functionally present, though the English framing is ungrammatical.

adjudicated.jp: 「……脳割れてるんじゃない？」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Didn't your brain split?"
adjudicated.assessment: The question whether his brain is split or cracked is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 割れてる。
adjudicated.en: It was split.
comments: It was split + it was made to split. This could mean it's broken; this could mean it's split as in a personality. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: In the manuscript's past-tense English narration, It was split is a valid deadpan confirmation. The audit's present-tense requirement conflicts with the adopted narrative frame.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic or grammatical revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺は楽しめたけどね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I managed to enjoy myself, though."
adjudicated.assessment: The statement that he managed to enjoy himself is preserved naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 「ふん」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Pah."
adjudicated.assessment: The dismissive snort is preserved by an established English interjection and bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「……楽しんだくせに（ぼそっ）」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...and you had fun too dammit. (whisper)"
adjudicated.assessment: The muttered accusation that she did enjoy herself is retained, but 'dammit' adds explicit profanity and heat absent from the trailing くせに and quiet ぼそっ delivery.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the muttered 'even though you had fun' accusation without added profanity.

adjudicated.jp: 「な・に・か・言った？」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "DID. YOU. SAY. SOMETHING?"
adjudicated.assessment: The menacing syllable-by-syllable emphasis is recreated through separated capitalized words.

adjudicated.jp: 「いいえなにも、サー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "No and nothing, SAH!"
adjudicated.assessment: The panicked denial and exaggerated 'sir' are preserved, despite the unnatural conjunction.

adjudicated.jp: 一週間の合宿。
adjudicated.en: One week of training camp.
comments: Later it will be an extended weekend. Unsure if it's intentional or just a (relatively minor) inconsistency. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment marking a week-long training camp is preserved exactly.

adjudicated.jp: ほんの幾度か、彼女の笑顔を見た。
adjudicated.en: And her smile I saw only a few times.
adjudicated.assessment: Seeing her smile only a few times is fully preserved; the inversion is stylistic awkwardness.

adjudicated.jp: 憮然とした顔つきがデフォルト設定の冬子だ。
adjudicated.en: A disappointed face is in Touko's default settings.
comments: The computer terminology begins! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 憮然とした here describes a sullen, displeased, or indignant expression, not disappointment. The English assigns a different emotional state to the character's default face.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'sullen,' 'displeased,' or an equivalent default scowl.

adjudicated.jp: 楽しんだに違いないのだ。
adjudicated.en: But she had fun, no mistake.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's certainty that she must have enjoyed herself is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: だってテント張って機材並べて。
adjudicated.en: After all, with all the tents spread and the machine parts set up,
comments: 機材 is the term used for the generic "machinery" that is brought up from the Club Room to the Antenna on the rooftop. The Training Camp looks more mysterious by the minute. They had survival games from the sound of it, but what anything else involved is never seen. If only because the idea they'd actually train with equipment and everything sounds so off for people who can't even look at each other. But they did stay there for a time, didn't they. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 機材 means equipment or gear. 'Machine parts' narrows it to components of machinery, which the source does not say, and changes the image of equipment being laid out.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'equipment' or 'gear.'

adjudicated.jp: 合宿はまるで別世界みたいだったから。
adjudicated.en: the training camp looked like an entirely different world.
comments: All with me now. Come on, don't be shy! We're only getting started: *cough* annnd SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The explanation that training camp felt like an entirely different world is preserved; 'looked like' slightly favors appearance without changing the comparison.

adjudicated.jp: 「いてててててっ！？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "OwTchTchTchTch?!"
adjudicated.assessment: The rapid repeated cry of pain is recreated functionally, despite eccentric internal capitalization.

adjudicated.jp: 耳を引く力が強まった。
adjudicated.en: The Pulling Power on my ear got harsher.
comments: See CCX0001. This is the only other instance of this exact term. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The force pulling on his ear becoming stronger is preserved, although 'Pulling Power' and 'harsher' are ungainly choices.

adjudicated.jp: 林道を抜けて、広場に出る。
adjudicated.en: Out of the forest path we come out to a wide grove.
adjudicated.assessment: 広場 is an open area, clearing, plaza, or field. A grove is a cluster of trees, so the English reverses the spatial transition from leaving the forest road and emerging into open ground.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'clearing' or 'open area.'

adjudicated.jp: 光が満ちる。
adjudicated.en: The light is in the rise,
adjudicated.assessment: 光が満ちる means that light fills or floods the space. 'Is in the rise' is not an English rendering of that image and instead suggests an unrelated act of rising.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Light floods in' or 'The clearing fills with light.'

highlights.text: The light is in the rise,

adjudicated.jp: 輝かしい陽光。
adjudicated.en: a resplendent sunshine.
comments: These seems to be the only clue that this is dawn, or at least no later than 6-7, since it uses the evening graphics. This fits them getting down by 10-11, and therefore the loop connecting 11:31 to 18:07, since by the time they're out of the path it's apparently inexplicably evening. The problem is that this is Sunday, therefore the world should get reset to a point before they enter. But let's not go break the setting; it's all in Taichi's head in the first place, so it's pointless. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment describing brilliant or resplendent sunlight is preserved; the indefinite article is merely unidiomatic.

adjudicated.jp: 「撤収、もうだいぶ終わっちゃってる」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "The striking... it's mostly done by now."
comments: How long has he been away? Maybe the whole of CCZAS took place right there. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: In the camp context, 'striking' is an established term for dismantling the camp, and the observation that it is mostly finished is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「こらあっ、そこのおサボなふたりーっ」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Come ooon, you two slackers over theeere!"
adjudicated.assessment: The distant, drawn-out call to the two slackers is preserved energetically.

adjudicated.jp: 声がぽややーんと響いた。
adjudicated.en: A voice resounded with boioioinnng.
comments: He might be talking about some part of Misato's anatomy, but my research has brought up nothing. -GHSarcasm
adjudicated.assessment: The unusual resonant quality is retained, but ぽややーん suggests a hazy, dreamy, or airheaded softness. 'Boioioinnng' instead evokes a springy comic bounce and materially changes the voice image.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an effect suggesting a soft, dreamy voice carrying through the air.

adjudicated.jp: 独特の声質。
adjudicated.en: It's a peculiar tone of voice.
comments: Jokingly it's about boobs, less jokingly Misato is currently deeeeeep into her mask. That's why she sounds sorta happy and frisky when she's in fact distraught. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The distinctive quality of the voice is preserved by 'peculiar tone of voice.'

adjudicated.jp: 我らが部長だ。
adjudicated.en: It's the President of our Club's.
adjudicated.assessment: The identification as the club president is preserved despite the malformed possessive ending.

adjudicated.jp: 「私は違います私は！」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "That is not what I am doing it is not!"
comments: Formal, talking to a Senpai because grammar nazism requires pseudo-connectional formal linguistics in the proto-bezoidal teching tech tech techy tech. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The emphatic denial that she belongs among the accused pair is preserved pragmatically as a denial of doing what they are doing, though the English repetition is ungrammatical.

adjudicated.jp: 「やぁ、なにかＨそうなことやってますっ！？」
adjudicated.en: President: "Wah, are you doing something sexually perverted?!"
comments: Then again, Misato may be forcing this joke, and poorly. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The alarmed question about something that looks lewd is present, but Ｈそう is colloquial 'sexy/naughty-looking.' 'Sexually perverted' intensifies it into a categorical moral judgment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'something naughty' or 'something lewd-looking.'

adjudicated.jp: 「停学、停学ですよ～っ！！」
adjudicated.en: President: "Suspension, there will be a suspensiooo~n!"
comments: This was Misato's first nickname for Taichi. She seems to bring it out when flustered, see CCA0025C, also CCC4006. See also her brother's penchant for breaking out 'traitor'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated, drawn-out warning about suspension is preserved despite stiff English.

adjudicated.jp: 焦って震える部長の声。
adjudicated.en: The President's voice quivered in embarrassment.
adjudicated.assessment: The president's trembling voice is preserved, but 焦って marks panic, fluster, or agitation rather than specifically embarrassment. The English supplies a psychological cause not fixed by the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the voice trembling with fluster or panic without specifying embarrassment.

adjudicated.jp: 「わはは」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wahahah!"
adjudicated.assessment: The broad laugh is preserved and bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「こ、この匹夫……」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Y-, you sphincter..."
comments: Curiously, all versions have a variation on this line. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 匹夫 is a contemptuous term for a lowly, common, ignorant, or boorish man. It has no anatomical meaning; 'sphincter' substitutes an unrelated body part and destroys the insult's register.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'wretch,' 'boor,' 'base man,' or another contemptuous personal insult.

adjudicated.jp: 「いたっ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Owww!"
adjudicated.assessment: The short cry of pain is preserved with exaggerated spelling.

adjudicated.jp: ようやく解放された我が愛耳と、叩かれた頭を同時に撫でながら。
adjudicated.en: At the very instant she finally released Our Beloved Ear, I stroked it together with my beaten-up head, and meanwhile,
comments: She smacked him earlier, see above, but given the sound she probably hit him on release as well. See CCZAS and CCX0001: is his "madness" something physical that can be beaten out of him? (Likely no or not quite, but the question is repeatedly asked). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The finally freed, mock-beloved ear and struck head being rubbed simultaneously are preserved. Extra temporal phrasing and the dangling continuation are stylistic defects only.

adjudicated.jp: 笑み。
adjudicated.en: I smile.
comments: AKA "force it" -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The nominal image of a smile is converted to the narrator's act of smiling, a contextually safe presentation shift bound to the resolved occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 「ニシシ、いたい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "HehShehSheh, it hurts."
adjudicated.assessment: The mischievous laugh followed by the admission of pain is represented functionally, though the laugh spelling is eccentric.

adjudicated.jp: 「さー、仕事仕事っと♪」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, to work!, to work!♪"
adjudicated.assessment: The jaunty pivot back to work, repetition, and musical cue are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「この男は……」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Really this man..."
adjudicated.assessment: The exasperated trailing 'this man...' reaction is preserved despite the awkward added adverb.

adjudicated.jp: 軽く走る。
adjudicated.en: Running lightly,
adjudicated.assessment: The light run or jog is retained as a participial continuation into the next line.

adjudicated.jp: 「まったく……」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "Seriously..."
adjudicated.assessment: The trailing exasperated interjection is naturally represented by 'Seriously...'

adjudicated.jp: 冬子のため息が追いかけてくる。
adjudicated.en: chased by Touko's sigh.
adjudicated.assessment: The sigh following or chasing after the narrator is preserved as the completion of the preceding running fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 部長の背後には、みんながいた。
adjudicated.en: Behind the President's back, everybody was there,
adjudicated.assessment: The spatial fact that everyone was behind the president is present, but 'behind the President's back' is a fixed English idiom for acting without someone's knowledge and can introduce an unintended relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use the unambiguously spatial 'Behind the president stood everyone else.'

adjudicated.jp: 二人で、みんなのもとに。
adjudicated.en: In a duo in front of everyone.
comments: It's ambiguous whether this is Taichi and Misato or Touko and Taichi. In the first case, Youko is not here; in the latter, she is. Supposing intentionality. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: みんなのもとに marks movement toward or joining everyone. 'In front of everyone' replaces the destination with a static public position and changes the fragment's spatial relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Together, we headed over to everyone.'

adjudicated.jp: 「おーーーーーーーーいっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: Heeeeeeeey!!!"
comments: ーx8 annnd there come the trolls. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The long shouted call is preserved; the missing opening quotation mark is a mechanical defect.

adjudicated.jp: わけもなく呼びかける。
adjudicated.en: I address the crowd without a real reason.
adjudicated.assessment: Calling out to the group for no particular reason is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 広場で機材の後かたづけをしていた五つの顔が、一斉にこちらを向いた。
adjudicated.en: The faces of the five who were tidying up the equipment in the grove turned my way in unison.
